newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: NWE oil products firm, except sagging mogas.
newsitem.headline: NWE oil products firm, except sagging mogas.

text.p: NWE oil products were firmer on Friday, except gasoline which weakened further after a sharp fall of futures on Thursday, dealers said.

Eurograde gasoline barges traded at $198 fob ARA and at $202 fob Rotterdam for prompt loadings. Late June deliveries traded at $200 and $201. The trades were on average about $1 a tonne lower than the deals concluded late on Thursday.
Swaps, however, were about $4 a tonne down, at around $199 fob ARA for June. July remained $8/$9 a tonne lower.

Heating oil barges gained by about $1 a tonne as IPE futures strengthened. Premiums were unchanged, with offers at about IPE June +$1 fob Rotterdam. Bids were at least 50 cents below. The strength of the dollar against the mark continued to deter German buyers.
Fuel oil barges traded from $86.75 to $87.50 fob Rotterdam. Late morning offers were at $88, with bids at $87/$87.50. Some traders said bunker demand was healthy, but most disputed this claim.
"Bunker demand is not so good. (The strength) is really just the result of short-covering," one trader said.
